messages.author: ddc1fc70af730460
messages.subject: Can't use faceting anymore in the 0.9-0 version
parts:
Hi,

I may as well be missing something obvious here, but I seem to get a
regression since I upgraded to ggplot2_0.9-0:

library(ggplot2)
library(plyr)

# Personal case
df <- data.frame(x = runif(100), y = runif(100), z =
sample(LETTERS[1:4], replace = TRUE, size = 100))
ggplot(df) + geom_histogram(aes(x = x)) + facet_wrap(~ z)
# I get the following error: Error: is.integer(group) is not TRUE

# From the ggplot2 book, Fig 7.3, pp120-121
data(movies)
movies$decade <- round_any(movies$year, 10, floor)
qplot(rating, ..density.., data = subset(movies, decade > 1890), geom
= "histogram", binwith = 0.5) + facet_wrap(~ decade, ncol = 6)
# I get the following error: Error: is.integer(group) is not TRUE

> sessionInfo()
R version 2.14.1 (2011-12-22)
Platform: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (64-bit)

locale:
[1] LC_CTYPE=en_GB.UTF-8 LC_NUMERIC=C
[3] LC_TIME=en_GB.UTF-8 LC_COLLATE=en_GB.UTF-8
[5] LC_MONETARY=en_GB.UTF-8 LC_MESSAGES=en_GB.UTF-8
[7] LC_PAPER=C LC_NAME=C
[9] LC_ADDRESS=C LC_TELEPHONE=C
[11] LC_MEASUREMENT=en_GB.UTF-8 LC_IDENTIFICATION=C

attached base packages:
[1] stats graphics grDevices utils datasets methods base

other attached packages:
[1] plyr_1.7.1 ggplot2_0.9.0

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
[1] colorspace_1.1-0 dichromat_1.2-4 digest_0.5.1 grid_2.14.1
[5] memoise_0.1 munsell_0.3 proto_0.3-9.2 RColorBrewer_1.0-5
[9] reshape2_1.2 scales_0.1.0 stringr_0.6 tools_2.14.1

I'm reluctant to fill a bug as I'm not sure whether it's a regression
or simply the Xmas break festivities still messing my brain up.

Cheers,

Pierre

--
Scientist
Landcare Research, New Zealand

parts:
Pierre - I think this is actually the result of a bug that was fixed in the last few weeks. The source code has identified itself as 0.9.0 for a long while (since December 2010!), but there have been many of changes along the way.

Try re-installing latest version. Instructions here:
https://github.com/wch/ggplot2/wiki/Using-ggplot2-branches

-Winston

messages.subject: Conceptual confusion with geom_segment and aes regarding line color
parts:
Hi.

I finally was able to have the following code work the way I want it to but, after re-reading the ggplot2 book, don't understand why the use of color should not be inside the aes within the geom_segment call.  If I put it inside, then 'black' is added to the legend with the label 'black' but the lines from geom_segment plot purple (the last color in the active color table.  This makes no sense to me.  Can someone perhaps explain this behavior?  Thank you.

J.

x0 =  0.0  
y0 =-20.0
#
x1 = 34.7
y1 =  0.0
#
K = (y1-y0)/(x1-x0)
#
p1 = ggplot(C, aes(Salinity, dO18, color=Site))
p1 + geom_point() +
     geom_segment(xend=32,   x=x1, yend=y0,  y = y1, aes(legend=F, linetype=2), color="black") + 
     geom_segment(xend=22.5, x=x1, yend=y0,  y = y1, aes(legend=F, linetype=2), color="black") +
     geom_segment(xend=11,   x=x1, yend=y0,  y = y1, aes(legend=F, linetype=2), color="black") +
     geom_segment(xend= 0,   x=x1, yend=-16, y = y1, aes(legend=F, linetype=2), color="black") +
     xlim(min(C$Salinity),max(C$Salinity)) + ylim(min(C$dO18),max(C$dO18)) + 
     ylab(expression(paste(delta,{}^18*"O ("^o*"/"[oo]*")"))) + xlab('Salinity (psu)')

messages.subject: Re: Conceptual confusion with geom_segment and aes regarding line color
parts:
Hi John,

aes() maps aesthetics (such as color) to variables. So aes(color = "black")
maps color to a variable who's values are all the same (i.e., "black").
compare to aes(color = "someFunkyTextString") -- you'll get the same thing,
except for the different label in the legend. Again, the reason is that you
are mapping color to this variable, not setting it to a fixed value. If you
want to set an aesthetic to a fixed value, do so outside of the aes() call.
Outside of aes() color = "black" sets the color to black.

Hope that helps,

Ista
